items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: He said, 'No matter what you see me do, or what I do, don't you worry.' Do you know that he called at least a hundred piano players to play with me? James P. Johnson, Willie the Lion Smith, Donald Lambert , Meade Lux Lewis, Pete Johnson, da, da and da.

ctx.x: Clash By Night. Well, what happened was, Billy Rose called Barney Josephson and asked him to have me come up to the Diamond Horseshoe. And they wanted...they had a scene... the theme of the thing was they wanted a blues, you know what I mean, like "Rhapsody in Blue." Not that kind of thing but th suggested, you know, kind of thing, you know, blues throughout, you know, that blues mood, and sad, and tragic... lonesome music.

So Billy Rose wasn't at the Diamond Horseshoe. They asked me to come over to his house on Sutton Place. So I went over to Billy's house and we became like father and son, or brother...two brothers. So he says, "Sam, now I'll tell you. I don't care what happens, you got the job." He wanted two piano players. "You got one of the jobs. Don't worry." He said, "No matter what you see me do, or what I do, don't you worry." Do you know that he called at least a hundred piano players to play with me? James P. Johnson,…
Billy was...oh, he was some showman. 'Course, wait 'til I tell you what Tallulah Bankhead did to him. He wanted untrained sound. He wanted it to be primitive,
